result.title: Replaying the Movie in Your Mind Decoding Dynamic Visual Perception and Recall from EEG
result.summary: Decoding dynamic visual content from EEG has advanced rapidly for visual perception, yet it remains unclear which aspects of neural representations are preserved when people internally replay dynamic scenes. We introduce PAIR, an EEG benchmark collected from 20 participants using an interleaved, clip-wise paradigm that pairs naturalistic video viewing with immediate visual recall. This design enables a comparison between externally driven perception and internally generated recall for the same stimulus content within a fixed trial sequence. We benchmark multiple decoding models on hierarchical semantic classification at both fine-grained and coarse-grained levels, meta-feature decoding tasks covering motion, color, object number, face, and human presence, and a state-decoding task that discriminates perception from recall. Within-subject validation results show numerically similar performance for several model--task combinations, alongside higher perception accuracy in two coarse-grained comparisons after multiple-comparison correction. In contrast, perception and recall are highly separable at the state level under the present validation protocol. State accuracy remains high after alpha-band ablation, although this does not exclude ocular or other task-related contributions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PAIR 脑电基准，用 20 名被试的交替片段范式把自然视频观看与即时视觉回忆配对，评测层级语义分类、运动/颜色/人脸等元特征解码以及「感知 vs 回忆」状态判别。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作探测内部自发重现的状态中保留哪些视觉内容、并区分内部生成与外部驱动状态，可为 LVR 中「内部状态是否保留视觉细节」「答案是否真正使用 latent 内容」提供可核查的类比与评价思路。
